notes: Every documented OpenAPI operation must be consumed by the frontend, mechanically derivable as a springdoc alias duplicate, or listed here with a category and a reason.
bff-route-handler and non-browser-consumer entries are machine-verified: an evidence file must exist and reference the operation path suffix. A category label alone proves nothing.
unwired entries are real debt. expected.unwiredMax is a monotonic ratchet — raising it is a visible diff, never a silent exception.
Alias duplicates (springdoc _N suffixes over multi-path @RequestMapping) are derived, never listed. Listing one is an error.

AXIS 2 (screen reachability): consumed on axis 1 only means a production TypeScript module calls the operation. Axis 2 additionally checks that the service method wrapping that call site is invoked from outside services/ and tests — the case that first exposed the gap was deleteRespondent, whose only caller was its own unit test.

Axis 2 keeps no exception list on purpose: 77 entries would become a drawer (H2). It is a single monotonic ratchet (expected.screenOrphanMax) and prints the full offending list on failure, mirroring status-color-guard.

Axis 2 is deliberately lenient, following UnreachableServiceLinter: a method counts as reachable if `.name(` appears anywhere in non-service production code. Common names may pass by collision — that direction misses violations rather than inventing them.

AXIS 3 (write affordance, 2026-10-01): a screen that calls a non-GET operation must use that operation's permission for display (the permission code appears in the file, in every screen that opens it, or the route itself guarantees it). Admin screens were brought to zero; expected.ungatedWriteMax freezes the remaining self-service screens (notes, comments, approvals, scraps, department work) and must equal the measured count in both directions.
Axis 3 is a display check only. Server authorization is unchanged, and a permission literal proves the screen looked at it, not which button it gates.

entries.note: Application-level liveness surface. PD-OPS-003 decided (2026-09-08) to keep the production compose healthcheck pointed at /actuator/health, which also covers registered indicators (DB, disk) — this endpoint only confirms the application answers. Retiring it was considered and deferred because external load balancers or monitoring may already target the path; that needs deployment-environment confirmation, not a repository decision.

Login-ID duplicate pre-check. DEC-OPS-135 bound it to USER_CREATE, so it is no longer an anonymous enumeration path. The admin user form has no pre-check: insertUser rejects a taken ID with DUPLICATE_USER_ID on save. Wiring a pre-check into that form is feature work, not a missing consumer of an existing flow.

The single-menu POST was used only by the board creation wizard, which registered an inactive admin-only menu right after creating the board. ADR-0043 decision 1 separated board creation from menu linking: the wizard now creates the board only, and menus are attached in menu management through the screen handoff, which saves with the versioned menu structure (depth check, sensitive-operation ledger). MenuAdminService.createMenu was removed with its only caller. Retiring the endpoint itself is a backend decision — see GAP-WIRING-001.

The legacy authority→menu "creation" surface predates the explicit NAVIGATION grants of ADR-0016. The menus-by-authority screen reads groups and their menus through getAuthors and getAuthorMenus, and grants are saved through the versioned authorization API or the menu structure draft. This handler calls the two-argument MenuService.insertMenuCreatList, which always rejects with INVALID_INPUT_VALUE and points to the unified authorization screen, so it cannot succeed. DEC-OPS-352 removed the dead MenuAdminService.saveMenuCreation; retiring the endpoint is a backend decision — see GAP-WIRING-001.
Self-notification creation for the authenticated principal. Admin dispatch to other users goes through the separate /admin/notifications/dispatch operation (DEC-OPS-042), which is wired.

ADR-0040 §5.2: the board list absorbed the single deactivation into the bulk use-flag change, which lists the app uses of each board (notice/FAQ/work-home designations and the knowledge hub tabs that open it) before confirming, and the operations screen settings tab saves the use flag with the board version. Both reach the same state (useYn='N') and record the USE change history. The single DELETE stays for API clients — it is a no-op when the board is already unused and otherwise records the change and bumps the version — but the dead BoardAdminService.deleteBoardMaster was removed.

ADR-0040 §5.2: permanent deletion left the board list toolbar and became a one-board procedure in the operations screen settings tab (deletable check, then DELETE …/physical). Bulk permanent deletion from a list is no longer a screen task; the dead BoardAdminService.batchDeleteBoardMastersPhysically was removed and the batch endpoint stays for API clients.

Common code classification delete. The server performs a logical delete (CommonCodeCategory.delete() sets useYn='N'), and the classification edit form already exposes a use-flag toggle that reaches the same state through updateClCode (CommonCodeCategory.update(..., useYn, ...)). update is in fact the better path because it also records lastMdfrId. DEC-OPS-068 verified both entity methods before retiring the dead frontend delegate; the HTTP surface stays.

Common code group delete. Same shape as deleteClCode — CommonCodeGroup.delete() sets useYn='N' and the group edit form reaches the same state through updateCmmnCode, which additionally records lastMdfrId. The dead frontend delegate was retired in DEC-OPS-068 after checking both entity methods; the HTTP surface stays.

DEC-OPS-208/209: the menu screen saves structure, properties, deletions and group visibility as one versioned draft through saveMenuStructure (PUT /admin/system/menus/structure). The per-menu update, batch reorder and delete endpoints remain for API clients but no screen calls them; the dead frontend service methods were removed so this is a superseded surface, not a missing feature.
ADR-0025 D09 moves the administrator screen to explicit whole-submission cancellation. The legacy single-row endpoint is retained as a compatibility surface; it is not the new screen task.

Authorized authorization simplification routes this workflow to the canonical versioned authorization API. Users may belong to multiple groups; department changes apply ADD/REMOVE deltas and group deletion is an explicit single-group operation. Legacy unversioned/bulk replacement is no longer exposed by the frontend. See docs/02-architecture/authorization-simplification-design.md.

The user/organization hub now consumes getDeptTree for the complete department hierarchy, replacing the paged getDepts client that imposed a 1,000-row cap. DeptApiController delegates both operations to DeptManageService.getDeptManageList; getDeptTree uses Pageable.unpaged() with the same keyword filter. The unused frontend getDeptList wrapper is retired, while the paged HTTP API remains compatible for external callers. See docs/archived/source-simplification-results-2026-10-06.md.

Institution code detail. The institution code screen renders from getInstitutionCodeList and never fetches a single row. The ledger itself is written only by direct DB loading: the unrouted write paths were removed on 2026-10-07 and PD-CODE-001 keeps the receive log read-only because chg_se_cd has no authoritative value domain — see GAP-CODE-001.

Notification detail — the notification centre renders from the list response and never fetches a single item.
